title: Extraction and quantification of lead in meconium: Analysis through inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometer (ICP-MS)
author: Neelotpol, Hay, et al.
materials: Prior to analysis it was important to make sure that all glassware and flasks were free from lead. Flasks (50ml), glass tubes (75 mm), and polypropylene tubes (12×50 mm) were washed and soaked overnight in 3% nitric acid, with all efforts made to ensure that all components were fully submerged in the acid. Tubes and flasks were rinsed six times with de-ionised water and the items allowed to air dry within a closed drying chamber.

steps.title: Clean all glassware and tubes
steps.instruction: Wash 50 mL flasks, 75 mm glass tubes, and 12 × 50 mm polypropylene tubes, then soak them overnight in 3 % (v/v) nitric acid ensuring complete submersion; rinse each item six times with de‑ionised water and air‑dry in a closed drying chamber.

substeps.instruction: Wash each flask, tube, and tube with detergent and rinse.
Soak overnight in 3 % nitric acid, fully submerging all pieces.
Rinse six times with de‑ionised water.
Place in a closed drying chamber to air‑dry.

steps.title: Dry meconium to constant weight
steps.instruction: Place 200 mg of hydrated meconium into an acid‑washed glass specimen tube and heat at 100 °C for 6 h (optimal; alternative tests at 50 °C, 80 °C, and 100 °C for 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, and 24 h) until a consistent weight is achieved; note that moisture loss can range from 29 % to 80 %.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 200 mg hydrated meconium into an acid‑washed glass tube.
Heat at 100 °C for 6 h (or test other temperatures/times as listed).
Weigh after each interval until weight stabilises.

steps.title: Prepare lead calibration standards
steps.instruction: Prepare lead standards at 0.25, 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 5, 10, and 20 µg L⁻¹ using the 1 mg L⁻¹ lead working solution.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the 1 mg L⁻¹ stock to each target concentration.
Verify concentrations with the ICP‑MS before sample runs.

steps.title: Spike meconium with lead standard
steps.instruction: For recovery experiments, weigh 2 g of dried meconium and add either 400 µL, 600 µL, or 800 µL of the 1 mg L⁻¹ lead working solution; 600 µL provides a free‑flowing mixture and is adopted for routine spiking.

substeps.instruction: Add 400 µL lead solution to 2 g meconium (viscous, poor mixing).
Add 600 µL lead solution to 2 g meconium (free‑flowing, optimal).
Add 800 µL lead solution to 2 g meconium (semi‑liquid).
Select 600 µL for subsequent experiments.

steps.title: Digest meconium with concentrated HNO₃
steps.instruction: Add concentrated nitric acid (purity > 69 %) to the spiked meconium (e.g., 100 mg sample) using volumes between 5 mL and 10 mL, vortex vigorously, and allow digestion for 20–30 min.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 5–10 mL concentrated HNO₃ onto the sample.
Vortex vigorously to mix.
Incubate for 20–30 min to complete digestion.

steps.title: Evaporate, filter and re‑suspend digest
steps.instruction: Ignite the digested mixture to reduce the volume to 1–2 mL, filter the concentrate, vortex the filtrate, then suspend the dried sample in 2 mL HNO₃, vortex and sonicate briefly.

substeps.instruction: Heat/ignite to evaporate to 1–2 mL.
Filter the reduced‑volume digest.
Vortex the filtrate to ensure homogeneity.
Add 2 mL HNO₃ to the dried sample, vortex, and sonicate briefly.

steps.title: Dilute extract with 1 % HNO₃
steps.instruction: Add 1 % nitric acid to the 2 mL extract in a 1:10 sample‑to‑acid ratio (i.e., add 18 mL of 1 % HNO₃ to make a total volume of 20 mL).

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 % HNO₃ solution.
Add 18 mL of this solution to the 2 mL extract.

steps.title: Analyze sample by ICP‑MS
steps.instruction: Aspirate 2 µL of the diluted solution into the Agilent 7700 ICP‑MS for lead quantification.
